result.summary: Replaces Boost.Test with an in-house, header-only unit test runner implemented in src/test/util/framework.{h,cpp}. Assertion macros support expression decomposition to print operand values on failure while retaining BOOST_* compatibility aliases so existing test suites do not need wholesale refactoring. Boost.Test dependencies and workarounds are simultaneously removed from CMake, Guix, depends, and vcpkg.
result.problem: Boost.Test introduces dependency maintenance burdens, including recurring platform-specific bugs and build workarounds. Test authors also face fragmented assertion macros (BOOST_CHECK, BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL, BOOST_TEST) that produce inconsistent error diagnostics and fail to print values for custom Bitcoin types without specialized operator overloads.
evidence: Author description highlights inconsistent failure reporting across Boost assertion macros and lack of helpful debug output for custom types like COutPoint.
Issue #8670 and #34666 document recurring community interest in dropping Boost.Test dating back to 2016.
Pull request #36045 shows recent dependency friction from Boost.Test signal stack sizing issues.

enables: Future migration of unit tests from legacy BOOST_* aliases to native CHECK and REQUIRE macros without merge conflicts.

result.scope_notes: Although the PR touches 166 files, most changes are produced by a scripted-diff replacing boost/test includes with test/util/framework.h. The substantive logic is contained in src/test/util/framework.{h,cpp} (~1,300 lines) and build configuration updates across CMake, depends, and Guix.
result.changed_since_previous: Added handling for expression decomposition limitations by wrapping bitwise and logical operators in macro calls, enforced stringify support or explicit opt-out with CHECK_NO_DISPLAY, added stream operator overloads for common test types, and inlined CRecipient initialization to bypass a GCC 12 warning.
result.card: This pull request replaces Boost.Test with an in-tree header-only test runner featuring expression decomposition and backward-compatible BOOST_* macro shims. Today, unit tests suffer from Boost.Test assertion quirks that inconsistently hide operand values on failure, alongside build-system overhead and platform workarounds in Guix and depends. Removing Boost.Test addresses recurring dependency issues and long-standing repository goals dating back to 2016 (#8670, #34666). The vast majority of the 166 touched files are purely mechanical include updates handled by a scripted diff.

risk.why: Mistakes are confined to unit test execution and test builds, with no effect on release binaries or node operation.
